title: Gold and commodities
blurb: What a commodity is, why gold pays nothing by itself, and what a making charge costs you.
t1.title: Raw goods
t1.hook: A wheat farmer fears the price will fall before harvest. A baker fears it will rise. Your mission: see how they can agree on a price today.
t1.define: A **commodity** is a basic raw good, like gold, wheat or oil. One unit is much like another. A **commodity exchange** is a regulated marketplace where standard contracts for commodities are traded.
t1.analogy: The farmer and the baker agree today on a price for next season's wheat. Both know what they will get and what they will pay.
q1.prompt: Which of these is a commodity?
q1.opt.a: Wheat, a basic raw good where one unit is much like another
q1.hint: Reread the definition at the top of this task.
q1.explain: A commodity is a basic raw good, like wheat, gold or oil.
q2.prompt: What does a commodity exchange do?
q2.opt.a: It is a regulated marketplace where standard commodity contracts are traded
q2.opt.b: It sets the price of gold by law
q2.opt.c: It makes trading commodities an easy way to earn money
q2.fb.c: Trading is not easy money. Prices move fast, and many traders lose.
q2.hint: Think about the farmer and the baker meeting in one place.
q2.explain: An exchange is a regulated marketplace for standard contracts.
t2.title: Gold earns nothing by itself
t2.define: Gold pays no interest and no dividend. You gain only if its price rises. The price can stay flat or fall for years.
t2.note: People hold gold out of tradition, and as a store of value in scary times. That does not make it a sure winner.
q3.prompt: How can you make money from gold you hold?
q3.opt.a: Only if its price rises above what you paid
q3.explain: Gold pays nothing by itself. You gain only if the price rises.
q4.prompt: Gold has risen for three years. What can you say?
q4.opt.a: Nobody can promise it will keep rising, and it can stay flat or fall for years
q4.opt.b: It always goes up, so it will keep rising
q4.fb.b: Gold does not always go up. It can stay flat or fall for years.
q4.hint: Can anyone promise a direction for a price?
q4.explain: Past rises promise nothing. Prices can stay flat or fall for years.
t3.title: The making charge
t3.hook: Asha buys gold jewellery for {price}. The shop adds a making charge of {charge}.
t3.define: A **making charge** pays for crafting the jewellery. It is part of the price you pay. It is not gold, and it usually does not come back when you sell.
t3.formula: Rise needed to break even = making charge ÷ (1 − making charge). Example: a 10% charge needs 0.10 ÷ 0.90, about 11.1%.
t3.explore: Open the lab. Keep the making charge at {charge}. Set the gold price change to +{rise}.
q5.prompt: How much of the {price} is making charge? Type a number in rupees.
q5.hint: The making charge rate times the price.
q5.explain: {charge} of {price} is {chargeAmt}. That part is not gold.
q6.prompt: The gold price rises {rise}. If Asha sells, what is the jewellery worth? Type a number in rupees.
q6.hint: Only the gold part grows. Read the value if you sell in the lab.
q6.explain: The gold part is {content}. After a {rise} rise it is worth {sellVal}, still below the {price} she paid.
q7.prompt: By what percent must the gold price rise just to get her {price} back? Type a percentage.
q7.hint: In the lab, slide the price change until your result stops being negative.
q7.explain: Only {content} of her money is gold. It must rise by about {breakeven} to be worth {price} again.
q8.opt.a: Gold jewellery has costs, such as the making charge, that you may not get back
q8.opt.b: Gold has no costs at all
q8.opt.c: Making charges are refunded in full on resale
q8.opt.d: A making charge is a gift from the shop
q8.fb.b: Gold has costs, such as the making charge. They can eat into any gain.
q8.hint: Look at the red box in the lab.
q8.explain: Jewellery carries costs. A making charge usually does not come back when you sell.
t4.title: Ways to hold gold
t4.define: Jewellery has a making charge and a deduction when you sell. Coins and bars usually cost less to make. Paper or digital gold has its own small costs.
t4.tradeoff: No way of holding gold is free. Compare the costs, and how easily you can sell, before you decide.
q9.prompt: Which way of holding gold usually has the lowest making cost?
q9.opt.c: None, because making is always free
q9.opt.d: They all cost exactly the same
q9.hint: Which one needs the least crafting?
q9.explain: Coins and bars need little crafting, so they usually carry a lower making cost.
glossary.commodity.def: A basic raw good, such as gold, wheat or oil.
glossary.commodity_exchange.def: A regulated marketplace where commodity contracts are traded.
glossary.making_charge.def: The fee for crafting jewellery. It is not gold.
glossary.purity.def: How much of the metal is pure gold, measured in carats.
